cards.title: Biorthogonal normalization and equality of four Chern numbers
cards.role: Defines the two-dimensional topological invariant and proves it is independent of left/right Berry-connection choice.

checks.reason: The four curvatures, normalization convention, and equality statement are explicit in the main text; the patch proof is explicit in Supplement II.
The LR and RR patch transformations share i grad(f); the extra grad(log r) has zero integral around a closed patch boundary, and the same argument closes LL/RL.
For a complex-symmetric Hamiltonian left and right states coincide up to conjugation, reproducing the stated zero-curvature limit.

cards.numerical_form: Analytic proof; optional lattice discretization of biorthogonal links is supporting evidence only.

cards.title: Generalized non-Hermitian Dirac spectrum and exceptional-point positions
cards.role: Generates the continuum bulk spectra, separability boundary, phase diagram, and exceptional-point trajectories.

checks.reason: Hamiltonian, spectrum, separable condition, and EP position formula are explicit in the main TeX.
Pauli algebra gives (d dot sigma)^2=(d dot d)I and expansion of d dot d reproduces every real and imaginary term.
The perpendicular EP displacement is real only for |m|<kappa and vanishes at |m|=kappa, reproducing EP-pair and hybrid-point boundaries.

cards.numerical_form: Vectorized complex radicand and its two square-root sheets; closed-form EP coordinates.

cards.title: Continuum domain-wall determinant and spinor matching
cards.role: Defines the independently solvable domain-wall edge spectrum used by Main Fig. 1 and Supplement Fig. 2.

checks.reason: The exponential ansatz, common-energy equation, spinor ratio, and localization inequalities are printed in the paper and supplement.
Replacing -i partial_x by -i/lambda in each half-space and taking the 2x2 determinant yields the stated squared-energy equation; component division yields the continuity ratio.
At kappa_y=delta=0 with opposite masses the equations reduce to the real chiral edge dispersion E=s_2 k_y and the printed localization lengths.

The algebraic solution satisfies the common-spinor determinant, both half-space characteristic equations, and localization signs; Supplement Fig. 2 points agree with independent nonlinear roots to 6.20e-16.

cards.numerical_form: Solve the common-spinor condition algebraically for both inverse localization lengths and the shared energy, select the branch by localization signs, and independently cross-check representative points with a nonlinear root solve.

cards.title: Energy-difference vorticity and canonical exceptional-point dispersion

source_refs.value: paper-source/nonHermitian.tex:140-169; main Eqs. (8)-(10) and Fig. 2 caption

cards.role: Generates all Main Fig. 2 panels and tests eigenvalue swapping and half-integer exceptional-point charge.

checks.reason: The vorticity definition, canonical Hamiltonian, loop, cut, and leading square-root dispersion are explicit in the main text.
With sigma_+=sigma_x+i sigma_y, det(EI-H)=E^2-[kx^2+ky^2+2kx+2i ky].
On k=(cos theta,sin theta), the radicand 1+2 exp(i theta) winds once around zero, so its continuous square root changes sign and has half winding magnitude.

cards.numerical_form: Evaluate analytic sheets on loop/surface/cut grids, unwrap the loop phase, and cross-check sampled points against direct 2x2 eigendecomposition.
open_questions: Vorticity sign is orientation-dependent; the case reports the loop orientation and tests the invariant magnitude.

cards.title: Square-lattice non-Hermitian cylinder Hamiltonian
cards.role: Defines the open-x, periodic-y cylinder spectra and chiral edge branches in Supplement Fig. 3.

checks.reason: The lattice Hamiltonian and all n=40 caption parameters are explicit in Supplement IV.
Forward/reverse blocks sigma_z/2 plus/minus sigma_x/(2i) Fourier transform to cos(kx)sigma_z+sin(kx)sigma_x.
At kappa=delta=0 the model is Hermitian and the stated |m|=2 gap closings follow at high-symmetry momenta.

cards.numerical_form: Build a 2n-by-2n block-tridiagonal complex matrix for each k_y and diagonalize values/eigenvectors.

cards.title: Hybrid-point dispersion from two merging exceptional points
cards.role: Generates the hybrid-point surfaces and demonstrates square-root versus linear directional scaling.

checks.reason: The merging condition, m=delta=1 parameters, loop radius, and two cuts are explicit in the main text and supplement.
Squaring H=(kx+i delta)sigma_x+ky sigma_y+m sigma_z and setting m=delta cancels the constant terms and gives the printed radicand.
At ky=0 the leading magnitude is proportional to |kx|^(1/2); at kx=0 the exact result is |E|=|ky|.

cards.numerical_form: Vectorized complex square-root sheets plus log-log exponent fits on the two symmetry cuts.
open_questions: The 3D view is not numerically specified; camera mismatch is a pixel-fidelity issue only.

cards.title: Codimension-two degeneracy and generic defectiveness
cards.role: Explains why generic non-Hermitian degeneracies occur in two dimensions and why the Fig. 2 origin is exceptional.

checks.reason: The general 2x2 form, two degeneracy equations, and nilpotent normal form are explicit in Supplement V.
Separating real and imaginary parts of (b0+i b1)^2=0 yields exactly two real scalar constraints.
For b nonzero, b sigma_+ is rank one and nilpotent, so its algebraic multiplicity two has geometric multiplicity one.

cards.numerical_form: Rank, nilpotency, and eigenvector-nullity checks on the canonical 2x2 matrix.
